source: REAL data (lab testbed) — intrusion=1: the flow belongs to a staged attack (Attack_type is anything other than MQTT_Publish, Thing_Speak or Wipro_bulb). Source: B. S. Sharmila and Rohini Nagapadma. RT-IoT2022 [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2023. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5P338 — described in "Quantized autoencoder (QAE) intrusion detection system for anomaly detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using RT-IoT2022 dataset", Cybersecurity (2023). What it is: real network flows (Zeek + Flowmeter) captured on a real IoT testbed — ThingSpeak-LED, Wipro bulb and MQTT temperature-sensor traffic as normal, and attacks STAGED by the researchers with standard tools (hping3 SYN flood, Slowloris, Nmap scans, ARP poisoning, Metasploit SSH brute force); lab traffic, not a production network. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — redistribution of this subset is permitted with attribution. Rows: 123,117 published, 5,195 exact duplicates removed, 117,922 usable (105,907 positive, base rate 89.81%). Features: flowSeconds, fwdPkts, bwdPkts, fwdDataPkts, bwdDataPkts, pktsPerSec, downUpRatio, synFlags, rstFlags, finFlags, ackFlags, fwdPayloadAvg, bwdPayloadAvg, fwdInitWindow, bwdInitWindow (Zeek flow fields, as published) and isUdp (proto udp=1). Ports, the service name and the scenario index are left out (artefacts of the testbed, not behaviour). Split: by capture order inside each scenario — for every traffic type the first 70% of its flows (by the published per-scenario index, after de-duplication) are the training split and the last 30% the held-out split; case mix fixed at 25.00% positive on BOTH sides by thinning the positive class evenly (deterministic, order kept); the population rate is 89.81%. The brain grew on 11,212 training rows only. This file: 1,500 of the 4,808 held-out rows, evenly spaced and class-stratified — 1,500 rows, 375 positive (25.00%); none were seen in growth.
